transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-25
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Marta (CSM), Jordan (Sparkline Head of Platform), Priya (Security), Ben (SRE), Ellen (PM)

Summary:
Quick kickoff/handoff between CS/SE to align on SSO integration, runbook updates for production ramp, and an initial perf benchmark/pilot timeline. Customer emphasized compliance items (KMS, audit logs) and wants a clear cutover plan for pilot -> prod.

Topics:
- SSO / SAML integration and SCIM for provisioning
- Private deployment network topology (VPC peering vs private link)
- Key management / encryption at rest and in transit (KMS/HSM)
- Performance expectations and bench plan for 5k sample workload
- Runbook changes: obs, alerting, rollback playbook, canary rules

Action items discussed (see metadata)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Aisha: Okay thanks everyone for joining, and uh yeah quick intros then we'll jump in. I'm Aisha on the Redwood AE team, joined by Samir our solutions engineer and Marta our CSM.
[00:12] Jordan: Hi all, Jordan here, head of platform at Sparkline. We've got Priya on security and Ben from SRE and Ellen from product. Thanks for making time.
[00:23] Aisha: Great, thanks. High level we want to handoff the work Marta's been tracking and sync on SSO and the prod ramp. Samir do you want to run through the technical plan?
[00:33] Samir: Yeah sure. So from the SE side, our recommended path is to start with hosted Redwood API for the pilot and then move to Dedicated if you need reserved capacity. But because you flagged compliance and private network requirements, we should plan the Private deployment option in parallel. That means we'll need CIDRs for VPC peering or we can do PrivateLink if you prefer that topology.
[00:54] Ben: We lean toward VPC peering right now because of our egress rules, but if PrivateLink is easier for the team we can evaluate. One question: do you require a full VPC in our account or is it a customer-managed peering?
[01:07] Samir: For Private deployment we support customer-managed VPCs and Redwood-managed endpoints. You keep control of the peering. We'll provide a template. There can be some nuance with route tables and NAT, we'll send a network checklist.
[01:21] Priya: On security — KMS is a hard ask for us. We need envelope encryption with our KMS, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, and SOC2 artifacts. Do you have an HSM integration?
[01:34] Marta: We do, and we can share the security pack. We have customers using both AWS KMS and third-party HSMs; there are options. We'll include the SOC2 report and details about audit log retention.
[01:46] Aisha: I'll drop the pack after the call. Priya, does Sparkline require on-prem key management or cloud KMS is fine?
[01:54] Priya: At pilot cloud KMS is okay but on the roadmap we may want HSM-backed keys for production. Need to confirm timelines.
[02:02] Ellen: From product's side, the main success criteria for the pilot are 1) latency p95 under 400ms for our 512-token prompts, 2) stable throughput for 10 rps burst, and 3) no data retention beyond request lifetime.
[02:18] Samir: That's reasonable. For p95 we can target hosted first, but for consistent p95 under load Dedicated with pinned model variants is more predictable. We can show benchmarking numbers from similar customers but we'll run your dataset too.
[02:33] Jordan: About model pinning — what level of control do we get? We need deterministic outputs across releases for compliance reasons.
[02:40] Samir: You can pin a model version and we support versioned rollouts. We also offer eval hooks so you can run regression tests on new model builds before rolling out. We'll document the pinning API.
[02:51] Ben: Also need to confirm how KV cache is handled during failover and whether sessions persist across backends. If we move from hosted to dedicated, do we lose cache?
[03:02] Samir: Good question. KV caches are per-instance; when you move backends you might not have hot cache warm. We have prefix caching and can warm caches during canary. We'll include recommendations in the runbook for cache warm-up and graceful fallback.
[03:16] Aisha: I want to surface the runbook items—Marta, you had a draft?
[03:20] Marta: Yes, I updated the onboarding runbook with sections for SSO, networking, bench plan, and rollback. We added an observability page with dashboard templates (latency, token counts, error rate) and runbook playbooks (canary failover, scale up). I'll share the doc link after this call.
[03:35] Jordan: Perfect. On SSO — we want SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning to reduce manual user creation. Also enforce Role Based Access Control (RBAC) mapped to our groups.
[03:46] Samir: We support SAML + SCIM. For RBAC we map your IdP groups to Redwood roles. There are edge cases with nested groups; we'll run a short mapping exercise.
[03:58] Priya: Any MFA or conditional access integration constraints? We need to ensure we don't bypass CA policies.
[04:04] Samir: We don't manage CA — it's handled by the IdP; we accept whatever tokens/assertions the IdP issues. SCIM provisioning is standard. We'll provide metadata and a test SP.
[04:18] Ben: Next, observability — what does the console expose for token-level cost and tracing? We need distributed tracing hooks to tie requests back to our request ids.
[04:27] Marta: The console includes per-route latency and cost breakdowns. For tracing, we support passing a trace id header which appears in logs and traces. We can provide an example integration with Datadog and OpenTelemetry.
[04:41] Ellen: Ok good. Now about timeline — we were hoping to pilot in mid-November. Is that achievable?
[04:48] Samir: If we start benching this week and get SSO metadata and VPC details this week, mid-November pilot is feasible. The critical path is SSO provisioning and network connectivity.
[04:59] Aisha: Let's list blockers — Priya, anything else on compliance?
[05:04] Priya: We need a clarified data retention policy and confirmation that user data isn't cached or logged beyond request TTL. Also export controls and data residency notes for EU users.
[05:14] Marta: We'll include the retention policy in the security pack and note EU regions availability. We can enable stricter retention per-customer.
[05:23] Jordan: For the perf bench, can we run a 5k sample set that mirrors our average prompt length? We want token distribution similar to prod.
[05:31] Samir: Yes, please provide a masked sample (PII removed) and we'll run bench and share the profiling: p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, and token cost.
[05:40] Ben: About cost — we need an estimate for tokens during pilot. Can you provide a rough monthly cost projection for 10k monthly users?
[05:49] Aisha: We can provide estimates; they'll vary by model and quantization. We'll include a cost sensitivity table for hosted vs dedicated with batching and cache parameters.
[06:02] Ellen: Any limits on streaming or function-calling behaviors? We use streaming to progressively render responses.
[06:09] Samir: Streaming is supported in hosted and dedicated. For private deployments streaming works but there are extra proxy timeouts to tune; we'll include recommended Nginx/proxy configs in the runbook.
[06:22] Priya: Back to KMS — does Redwood ever touch plaintext keys? We need separation of duties.
[06:28] Marta: No, we never persist plaintext keys. We use envelope encryption and can integrate with your KMS. We'll note key rotation procedures.
[06:36] Jordan: Can you walk us through the pilot success criteria one more time?
[06:40] Ellen: I'll list them: p95 < 400ms on 512 tokens, 99.9% availability during pilot window, audit logs shipped to our SIEM, SSO + SCIM operational, and a documented rollback plan.
[06:54] Samir: We'll map each criterion to an acceptance test and include it in the runbook checklist.
[07:00] Aisha: Let's define the cadence: weekly sync for the next 4 weeks, with a mid-week bench result review. Marta will run those.
[07:08] Marta: I'll set recurring invites and share agendas.
[07:12] Ben: One technical nuance — we use sidecar proxies that inject headers for tracing, will Redwood accept forwarded headers?
[07:19] Samir: Yes, we accept forwarded headers but you should ensure we trust the proxy. We'll add header allowlist docs.
[07:29] Jordan: Any special licensing or reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated? We need to present to procurement.
[07:36] Aisha: We have reserved capacity terms and monthly commits. For pilot we recommend hosted or a trial Dedicated allocation; we'll send a short pricing summary.
[07:48] Priya: On procurement — we need indemnification and data processing addendum. Who does legal talk to?
[07:55] Aisha: I'll connect your legal lead to our contracts rep. I'll include the DPA and SOW templates in the pack.
[08:05] Ellen: Great. Can Samir sketch a bench plan now? Rough steps and what you'll need?
[08:12] Samir: Sure. Step 1: customer shares masked sample dataset + expected RPS profile. Step 2: Redwood runs bench in a staging env over 24 hours simulating burst patterns. Step 3: share results and recommendations (batching, model/quantization). Step 4: iterate and tune network + proxy settings. We'll need an API key and a test workspace.
[08:36] Ben: Do you need us to open any ports or set up NAT? We'll provide CIDRs.
[08:40] Samir: We'll need peering config and security groups; I will provide a small template.
[08:47] Aisha: Ok folks, let's go around for any final clarifications. Priya?
[08:50] Priya: Just ensure the audit log retention period and format; we need JSON logs with certain fields - timestamp, request_id, user_id, model_version, and tokens_consumed.
[08:58] Marta: Noted. We'll include the exact schema.
[09:02] Jordan: From platform side, we'll prioritize VPC details and a masked sample by end of week.
[09:08] Ellen: I'll coordinate the sample and the product acceptance criteria doc.
[09:13] Ben: I'll pull CIDRs and mapping. Expect that by Friday.
[09:17] Aisha: Great. Quick recap of next steps: I'll send the security pack + SSO checklist; Samir will queue the perf bench once we receive a dataset; Marta will schedule weekly syncs. Anything else?
[09:29] Jordan: Could we also get a short live demo of the console focusing on observability and tracing? Preferably next week.
[09:35] Samir: Yes we can do a 30-min demo; Marta will propose slots.
[09:40] Aisha: Perfect. Thanks everybody. We'll follow up via the shared ticket and calendar invites.
[09:44] Meeting ends.
